description: The Phase 3 ELLI Data release documents quasi-static cyclic tests of a full-scale three-storey mass-timber building assembly at Oregon State University. Two test events compared the gravity system alone with a configuration that added self-centering rocking walls and U-shaped steel energy dissipators. The repository lists 469 public files under CC BY 4.0, including force, displacement and strain measurements, drawings, photographs and time-lapse video. The article describes three load cells, dozens of displacement sensors and thirty-two strain locations. Coverage is one controlled laboratory structure over two two-day test events, not a population of occupied timber buildings or earthquake field records. Loading protocol, connection details and the chosen wall system limit transfer to other designs. A reviewer-assessed simulation use is calibrating lateral-response or damage-state models for mass-timber structures. data-nees-soft-story-woodframe-hybrid-test is a related structural test collection with different construction. The drawings, sensor traces and video were not downloaded, and no seismic model was executed. A known limitation is that quasi-static loading does not reproduce the full frequency content of real earthquakes.
